subject: pushed 1-file R/Stan interface a la R2WinBUGS

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: pushed 1-file R/Stan interface a la R2WinBUGS
parts:
I pushed a very crude system-call-based R interface
to Stan in the form of a single file of function definitions
at the top level of the Stan release (I didn't want to mess up
Jiqiang's work on rstan):

r2stan_sys.R

(No -- we're not going to call anything r2stan, but I
couldn't think of what else to call it without confusing
it with the existing rstan.)

Its interface follows R2WinBUGS, and it returns
an R2WinBUGS "bugs object" (which can be printed,
attached, plotted, and the variables returned with
structure or converted into a Coda object).

It requires that Stan be installed (which in turn
requires a modern-ish C++ compiler and make to be installed),
and the bin/stanc parser and bin/libstan library be pre-built.
This is all documented in gory detail in the appendix and
getting started sections of our reference manual.

Like R2WinBUGS, it uses system calls to invoke Stan.

The drawbacks compared to the deeper integration Jiqiang's
undertaking is that file I/O vs. C++/R integration is slow,
especially with lots of processes (cores) running. The
use of R for storing the samples means more memory use.
It also means writing all the functionality to analyze
samples/chains in R.

The advantage is that Stan is completely independent of R
(and of Rcpp) when run this way -- we won't depend on their compilers,
their compiler options, versions of Boost, Eigen, etc. It also means
we won't crash the R session if Stan segfaults (tries to read memory
it shouldn't).

Another bonus is that using R to store the samples means they'll
save and restore easily. Also, piggybacking on R2WinBUGS
means instant Coda compatibility.

The ability to pull out just the named samples means
it'll be easy for Ilya to work on right away without
any direct dependency on Stan.

I think we'll be able to use some of the parallel
options in R to run chains on multiple cores pretty easily
(mclapply, in particular, looks promising). To do this
from R directly in rstan depends on our finding some cross-platform
threading option (maybe Boost).

The current version won't work on Windows -- the file
naming convention and names of executables need to
be finessed.

Here's the declaration of the main function
(there are also some support functions to do things
like write data or inits files once).

stan = function(model.file,
cpp.file = "anon_model.cpp",
model.executable = "./a.out",
samples.dir = "samples",
data = NULL,
inits = NULL,
chains = 3,
seed = floor(runif(1,0,100000000)),
iter = 2000,
warmup = iter / 2,
thin = max(1, floor((iter - warmup) / 1000)),
leapfrog_steps = -1,
max_treedepth = 10,
epsilon = -1,
epsilon_pm = 0,
unit_mass_matrix = FALSE,
delta = 0.5,
gamma = 0.05,
test_grad = FALSE,
cc = "g++ -O3",
stan.home = STAN_HOME) {

It requires stan.home be set in order to be able to find Stan and lets
you control the compiler using cc (it must be compatible with
whatever was used to make Stan). The other params should be familiar
from R2WinBUGS or from the Stan compiled model command doc.

I apologize in advance for the insanely clumsy R code. I'm sure
many of my loops would be one-liners for the pros.

I also need to think about how to add make-like functionality
so as not to have to recompile each go round. I had that in place,
but it wasn't making me happy when I changed models but stuck
with default intermediate file names.

Here's an example call to run the BUGS volume 1 example Rats
using their inits. This example takes the silly
step of reading the data into the top-level R environment from
a file and then creating a list, which it then writes to
a file to send to Stan -- you could just send the file in
directly, but I wanted to show that it also worked like
R2WinBUGS.
